Optional number. Higher = shown more often. Blank = 1.

intro.1/2/3, health.critical, health.unstable.up, health.unstable.down, health.healthy, health.thriving, notify.unlocked, hint.withReq.1-4, hint.fallback, species.overpopulated, species.overpredated, species.starving, species.extinct, species.added

Text: Hey, my name's Alucia!
As you can see, this ecosystem isn't doing too well...
Please help me save it!
The reef is collapsing, we're losing species fast!
It's falling apart out here, we have to act now!
It's stabilising a little... keep going!
Things are slipping, the balance is breaking down.
The reef's looking much healthier now!

Text: Uh oh, the {species} are overpopulating and nothing is keeping them in check! Try adding one of their predators to balance the reef.
Oh no, the {species} are being hunted too hard! Try removing one of their predators so they can recover.
The {species} have run out of food! Try adding some of the fish they like to eat.
Wow, there are so many Blacktip Reef Sharks! As the top hunter they need lots to eat. Try adding more prey like Fringelip Mullet or Yellowstripe Scad, or remove a shark or two to balance the reef!
The Blacktip Reef Sharks are the top hunters here, so nothing preys on them. If they look unhappy, it is usually because they are low on food!
Oh no, the Blacktip Reef Sharks are going hungry! They have nothing to hunt. Try adding some Fringelip Mullet or Yellowstripe Scad for them to eat!
Whoa, the Bluefin Trevally are taking over! They are a top hunter, so try adding more prey like Yellowstripe Scad for them, or remove a few to balance things out!
The Bluefin Trevally are fast top hunters, so nothing chases them. Keep an eye on their food instead!
The Bluefin Trevally are starving! Try adding some Yellowstripe Scad or Fringelip Mullet so they have something to hunt!
There sure are a lot of Brown Marbled Groupers! They are big hunters, so try adding more prey like Bullethead Parrotfish, or remove a grouper or two to keep balance!
The Brown Marbled Groupers are strong hunters with no predators of their own. If they struggle, check their food supply!
Uh oh, the Brown Marbled Groupers have run out of food! Try adding some Bullethead Parrotfish or Fringelip Mullet for them to eat!
So many Giant Morays! These sneaky hunters have no predators, so try adding more prey like Streaked Spinefoot, or remove a moray to balance the reef!
The Giant Morays are ambush hunters that nothing preys on. If they are unhappy, they are probably hungry!
The Giant Morays are hungry with nothing to hunt! Try adding some Yellowstripe Scad or Streaked Spinefoot to feed them!
Wow, the Bluespotted Ribbontail Rays are everywhere and nothing is hunting them! Try adding a Blacktip Reef Shark to keep their numbers in check!
Oh no, the Bluespotted Ribbontail Rays are getting eaten up fast! Try removing a Blacktip Reef Shark to give them a chance to recover!
The Bluespotted Ribbontail Rays find their food buried in the sand, so they never go hungry here!
Uh oh, the Bullethead Parrotfish are taking over the reef! Try adding a hunter like a Brown Marbled Grouper or a Bluefin Trevally to balance things out!
Yikes, the Bullethead Parrotfish are being hunted too hard! Try removing a Brown Marbled Grouper or a Bluefin Trevally so they can bounce back!
The Bullethead Parrotfish love scraping algae off the coral, so they always have plenty to eat!
So many Eyestripe Surgeonfish! With no predators around they just keep growing. Try adding a Giant Moray or a Russell's Snapper to hunt a few!
The Eyestripe Surgeonfish are disappearing fast, too many hunters are after them! Try removing a Giant Moray or a Russell's Snapper to give them a break!
The Eyestripe Surgeonfish graze on algae all day, so they always have plenty to munch on!
The Fringelip Mullet are booming and nothing is eating them! Try adding a Bluefin Trevally or a Brown Marbled Grouper to keep them balanced!
Oh no, the Fringelip Mullet are getting wiped out! Try removing a Bluefin Trevally or a Brown Marbled Grouper so they can recover!
The Fringelip Mullet sift tasty bits from the sand, so they always find enough to eat!
Whoa, the Reticulated Damselfish are everywhere! Try adding a Yellowstripe Scad or a Bluefin Trevally to snack on some and even things out!
The Reticulated Damselfish are vanishing fast! Try removing a Yellowstripe Scad or a Bluefin Trevally to ease the hunting!
The Reticulated Damselfish nibble on algae and plankton, so they never run out of food!
The Russell's Snappers are overpopulating and nothing is hunting them! Try adding a Giant Moray or a Blacktip Reef Shark to keep them in check!
Uh oh, the Russell's Snappers are being eaten faster than they can recover! Try removing a Giant Moray or a Blacktip Reef Shark to help them out!
The Russell's Snappers are going hungry! Try adding some Fringelip Mullet or Reticulated Damselfish for them to eat!
Too many Streaked Spinefoot! Try adding a hunter like a Giant Moray or a Bluefin Trevally to balance the reef!
The Streaked Spinefoot are getting hunted too hard! Try removing a Giant Moray or a Bluefin Trevally so they can recover!
The Streaked Spinefoot feast on algae and seagrass, so they always have plenty to eat!
The Yellowstripe Scad are exploding in number! Try adding a Bluefin Trevally or a Blacktip Reef Shark to hunt a few and balance things out!
Oh no! The Yellowstripe Scad are getting wiped out, too many hunters are after them! Try removing a Brown Marbled Grouper or a Bluefin Trevally to balance the ecosystem!
The Yellowstripe Scad have nothing to eat! Try adding some Reticulated Damselfish to feed them!
The {species} are gone from the reef entirely.
Without the sharks, nothing keeps the reef in balance. Watch what happens now!
A new group of {species} just swam in!

Text: Per-species 'fun fact' hint Alucia says while pointing to the next species to unlock. One is picked at random.
The reef shark needs a fully functioning food web to return.
You need Grouper x1, Moray x1, Trevally x2 and Scad x3.
Almost there, the shark is close to returning to the reef!
Fast predators like trevally prey on mullets and parrotfish
You need Mullet x3 and Parrotfish x2 to attract trevally.
Almost there, add more mullet and parrotfish.
Rays feed on the reef floor and need herbivores nearby.
You need Parrotfish x2 and Spinefoot x2 to attract rays.
Almost there, add more parrotfish and spinefoot.
Grouper are ambush predators that need schooling prey.
You need Scad x2, Trevally x1 and Snapper x1 to attract grouper.
Almost there, stabilise your secondary consumer population.
Parrotfish graze algae and keep coral healthy.
A stable parrotfish population supports larger reef predators.
More parrotfish will help attract secondary consumers.
Surgeonfish keep algae under control on the reef.
A stable surgeonfish population supports the next trophic level.
Add more surgeonfish to unlock secondary consumers.
Mullet are a key food source for larger reef predators.
Build up mullet numbers to attract secondary consumers.
Add more mullet to stabilise the base of the food web.
Moray eels hunt in reef crevices, targeting prey like Russell's snappers and parrotfish.
You need Snapper x2 and Ray x1 to attract the giant moray.
Almost there, build up snapper and ray populations.
Damselfish are small but vital prey for reef predators.
Build damselfish numbers to attract schooling predators.
More damselfish will unlock secondary consumers.
Snappers are ambush predators that need prey on mullets and damselfish.
You need Damselfish x2 and Surgeonfish x2 to attract snapper.
Almost there, build up damselfish and surgeonfish.
Seagrass meadows are the foundation of the reef, feeding grazers and giving fish shelter.
Healthy seagrass supports herbivores like parrotfish and surgeonfish.
More seagrass helps the whole food web thrive.
Spinefoot are algae grazers that support reef health.
Stable herbivores attract secondary consumers like rays.
Add more spinefoot to complete the primary consumer tier.
Schooling fish like scad love small fish like damselfish.
You need Damselfish x2 and Mullet x2 to attract scad.
